headline: Energy and copper surge while precious metals retreat on rate concerns
paragraphs: Natural gas led gains with an 8.98% surge to $3.05 per MMBtu (EUR 2.72), as European natural gas benchmarks surged to multi-year highs. WTI crude gained 3.99% to settle at $103.44 per barrel (EUR 92.32), driven by escalating fears of conflict in the Middle East.
Copper advanced 2.12% to $6.50 per lb (EUR 5.80), staging a rebound as global stock markets and inventory levels stabilized.

Conversely, precious metals fell sharply over the week. Silver slipped 1.47% on the day to $53.96 per oz (EUR 48.16), bringing weekly declines to 5.33%, while gold settled at $4,010.00 per oz (EUR 3,578.92) for a 4.09% weekly drop. The downturn in haven assets was driven by surging oil prices, which have stoked inflation expectations and bolstered bets on US Federal Reserve rate hikes. Palladium also dropped 6.00% this week to $1,046.50 per oz (EUR 934.00), though specific broader drivers behind the platinum group metal sell-off remain unclear.
